:::{#def-riemann-integral}
#### Riemann integral (definite integral)

Let $f$ be a [bounded](algebra.qmd#def-bounded) function on $[a, b]$.
For each partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $[a, b]$ (@def-partition),
choose a sample point $x_i^*$ in each subinterval $[x_{i-1}, x_i]$.
The **Riemann integral** of $f$ over $[a, b]$
[@wikipedia_riemann_integral]
(also called the **definite integral** of $f$ from $a$ to $b$)
is the limit of the Riemann sums (@def-riemann-sum) as the mesh (@def-mesh) shrinks to zero:

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx \eqdef \lim_{\norm{\mathcal{P}} \to 0} \sumin f(x_i^*)\,\change x_i,$$

when that limit exists and has the same value
for every choice of the partitions and of the sample points $x_i^*$.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 4.3, p. 272]

:::
